name: Gentamicin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Gentamicin is an aminoglycoside cleared by glomerular filtration; it is nephrotoxic and ototoxic (boxed warning), with higher risk in kidney impairment. The US label adjusts by serum creatinine (interval = serum creatinine × 8 hours, or a reduced-dose table) with serum-level monitoring, and gives 1 to 1.7 mg/kg at the end of each hemodialysis (2 mg/kg in children). Peritoneal dialysis removes it much more slowly than hemodialysis. Injection only: eye/ear drops and cream need no kidney dose adjustment.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses serum creatinine (mg/dL) with an approximate CrCl (mL/min/1.73 m2) table.
chip: Injection: nephrotoxic; adjust by SCr; TDM

bands.recommendation: Normal kidney function: 3 mg/kg/day in 3 doses every 8 hours; up to 5 mg/kg/day for life-threatening infection, reduced as soon as possible. Obese patients: dose by lean body mass. Measure peaks (4 to 6 mcg/mL) and troughs (label). Alternative (not in label): extended-interval dosing, e.g., 7 mg/kg with interval by CrCl (≥60: every 24 h; 40–59: every 36 h; 20–39: every 48 h) and a single-level nomogram (Nicolau 1995). Not validated below CrCl 20 or on dialysis: use the label method with levels.

After the usual first dose, either extend the interval (hours = serum creatinine in mg/dL × 8) or keep 8-hourly doses reduced by the label's serum creatinine table (Table 4) or by dividing the normal dose by serum creatinine. Avoid prolonged peaks above 12 mcg/mL and troughs above 2 mcg/mL; measure levels (label). Table 4 examples: CrCl about 40–45 (SCr 2–2.2): 50%; 30–35 (SCr 2.6–3): 35% of the usual dose every 8 hours. Alternative (not in label): extended-interval dosing, e.g., 7 mg/kg with interval by CrCl (≥60: every 24 h; 40–59: every 36 h; 20–39: every 48 h) and a single-level nomogram (Nicolau 1995). Not validated below CrCl 20 or on dialysis: use the label method with levels. In AKI, creatinine lags; the label warns that deteriorating kidney function needs a greater reduction than these tables.

hd.text: 1 to 1.7 mg/kg at the end of each dialysis, depending on severity of infection; an 8-hour hemodialysis lowers levels by about 50% (label). Check levels.

pd.text: No PD dose in label; removal by peritoneal dialysis is much slower than by hemodialysis. For PD-associated peritonitis (ISPD 2022): 0.6 mg/kg intraperitoneally once daily, intermittent (in one exchange daily with a dwell of at least 6 hours); continuous dosing is not advised. Check levels; specialist input.

crrt.text: No data in label, and gentamicin is not in the Li 2020 CRRT table. Level-guided dosing with specialist input.

dialyzable: Yes by hemodialysis (about 50% over 8 hours; label); much less by peritoneal dialysis. Protein binding 0% to 30%.
monitoring: Peak and trough levels; serum creatinine before and during therapy; urinalysis; hearing and vestibular function; magnesium, calcium and potassium (wasting, Fanconi-like syndrome reported). Avoid other nephrotoxic drugs and potent diuretics.

pediatric.approved_ages: Children, infants and neonates (label; this premixed bag may not suit small children).
pediatric.usual_dose: Children: 6 to 7.5 mg/kg/day (2 to 2.5 mg/kg every 8 hours). Infants and neonates: 7.5 mg/kg/day (2.5 mg/kg every 8 hours) (label).
pediatric.neonates: Premature or full-term neonates 1 week of age or less: 5 mg/kg/day (2.5 mg/kg every 12 hours) (label). Practice outside the US label: international neonatal guidelines vary from 4 to 6 mg/kg per dose every 24 to 48 hours; a model-based analysis proposed 7.5 mg/kg at 36- to 48-hour intervals set by gestational and postnatal age, with levels for courses beyond 3 days (van Donge 2018). Preterm infants need higher doses at extended intervals than term neonates (Fuchs 2014). With standard dosing, about half of neonates missed the target trough (1 mg/L or less) or peak (8 to 12 mg/L) (Hollander 2023). Check serum creatinine, and levels when treatment runs beyond 48 to 72 hours: unmonitored 5 mg/kg daily dosing was associated with acute kidney injury in a small study of term neonates (James 2024).

renal.recommendation: Label serum creatinine methods are not age-limited; monitor levels. Specialist input in children.

hd.text: Children: 2 mg/kg at the end of each dialysis (label). Check levels.

pd.text: No label dose; see ISPD 2022; specialist.

adult: Selected label is the Baxter premixed bag (2023); PH products are 40 mg/mL vials (plus ophthalmic/otic drops and cream). Kidney dosing is the same drug; consider pinning a vial label with pediatric 10 mg/mL text.
Label describes conventional 8-hourly dosing; extended-interval dosing is not in the label.
ISPD 2022 intraperitoneal gentamicin dose not stated (full text not read).
pediatric: Serum creatinine × 8 and Table 4 were derived in adults; a child's lower creatinine makes them less reliable. Kept as label wording.

revision_log.change: Extended-interval alternative (7 mg/kg; q24/q36/q48 h by CrCl ≥60/40–59/20–39; Nicolau 1995) and AKI caveat (label: deteriorating function) added.
Table 4 examples now inside the 30–59 band (CrCl 40–45: 50%; 30–35: 35%).
Chip 'Injection:'; summary notes drops and cream need no kidney adjustment.
PD tile: ISPD 2022 Table 5 IP dose for PD-associated peritonitis, 0.6 mg/kg IP daily intermittent (one exchange, dwell ≥6 h); continuous not advised.

Neonatal field: label dose kept; added a practice note on extended-interval dosing, targets and monitoring from four PubMed-verified studies (van Donge 2018, Fuchs 2014, Hollander 2023, James 2024). State hospital guidelines and tertiary references excluded per sourcing rules.
